explain.name: Supply
explain.measures: How much known production capacity is running
explain.sentence: Of the capacity we can document, roughly 36% appears available (estimate; no producer publishes run rates) - plants listed as shut: Jihua, Runtu, Yuyuan. No new plant accidents or shutdowns were reported in the last 90 days.

explain.name: Raw-material costs
explain.measures: Prices of naphthalene, sulfuric acid, nitric acid and caustic soda
explain.sentence: The raw-material price index moved -3% in the last month and -9% over three months, so costs are not what is driving H-Acid now. Sulfuric acid is -14% over three months but still +176% versus a year ago.

explain.name: Dye prices
explain.measures: Prices of the reactive dyes H-Acid is used to make
explain.sentence: Chinese reactive-dye shipments to dyeing countries that report imports (like-for-like) changed -50% over three months and -46% over a year to Jul 2026 - a sign of demand for the dyes H-Acid goes into.

explain.name: Exports
explain.measures: Price paid by foreign buyers (India, Korea, Indonesia) for Chinese H-Acid
explain.sentence: Foreign buyers paid about $9,237/t for Chinese H-Acid-type acids in Jul 2026 (+57% vs three months earlier, +73% vs a year earlier). Trade data arrives about two months late.

explain.name: Stockpiles
explain.measures: How much H-Acid is sitting in warehouses
explain.sentence: No reliable public stockpile data exists for H-Acid, so this is left blank rather than guessed.

explain.name: Textile demand
explain.sentence: No reliable public textile-demand series is collected yet.

explain.name: Plant events
explain.measures: Accidents, shutdowns and rule changes at factories
explain.sentence: The most recent recorded event was 191 days ago (policy); its effect has faded.

explain.name: Price trend
explain.measures: How fast the H-Acid price itself is moving
explain.sentence: The price rose +58% in the month to 08 Oct, but has not changed for 8 days (Chinese holiday), so short-term momentum is fading.

headline: Prices are holding at a record ¥150,000/t after a 146% surge that began on 28 Jul. No new price turn is building; falling raw-material costs are a mild pressure.

live.sentence: No statistically significant price inflection detected. Underlying pressure: cost relief (below inflection strength).
